title: Modular Hosted Endpoint PRD: Behavioral Requirements, Scope Change Log, and Launch QA Playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: This PRD defines a modular hosted inference endpoint surface covering Completions, Chat, Embeddings, and Rerank. It consolidates behavioral contracts, error semantics, rate-limiting expectations, and operational runbooks required for an initial GA launch and staged rollouts. Goals: 1) Provide a single, discoverable endpoint family with deterministic behavioral contracts for prompt/response patterns; 2) Define backward compatible parameter semantics so SDKs can surface minimal migration friction; 3) Provide launch quality gates (latency/cost/accuracy) and an operational canary plan. Non-goals: Multi-protocol adapters (gRPC) for GA, real-time streaming of rerank responses (post-GA), and automated model selection beyond simple tier routing.
scope: Included: REST API contracts for text/completions, chat turn semantics, embedding generation, and rerank scoring; SDK surface parity (Python/TS); acceptance test harness and canonical prompt sets for each capability; rollout canary with per-tenant QoS throttling. Excluded: Websocket streaming for rerank, gRPC surface, multi-region active-active for Dedicated at GA.
outcomes: - Clear behavioral contracts for each capability documented in Confluence and referenced in SDK README. - Acceptance test pass rate >= 98% on canonical prompt suites. - Latency SLOs met under canonical load profiles. - Production rollout with automated rollback on quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: API schema validated in contract tests with 100% coverage of required fields and parameter edge cases
Functional parity: sample SDK calls produce identical normalized outputs compared to reference harness for 95% of canonical prompts
Latency SLO: p95 request latency <= 250ms for Embeddings (small batch), <= 400ms for Completions (short context), <= 200ms for Rerank (single-query), under canary load
Throughput baseline: hosted-standby instances sustain 120 tokens/sec per vCPU-equivalent under continuous batching tests
Quality regression gate: evaluated against baseline evals with <1% degradation in retrieval/response relevance metrics
Operational metrics: end-to-end tracing and token-level cost breakdowns available in Console for the canary tenants
Security: KMS key binding and audit-log events validated for Private-linked tenants where applicable
Rollout: automated canary for 2% of traffic with rollback hook on error rate >1% or quality regression triggered
launch_checklist: Finalize API behavioral document and publish Confluence page: /docs/hosted-unified-endpoints
Complete SDK parity PRs (Python and TS) and merge: GH PRs linked below
Run full acceptance harness across models and quantization profiles; record results in acceptance dashboard
Provision canary tenant list and configure rate-limits/quotas for staged rollout
Coordinate Dedicated capacity reservations and autoscaling policies with Infra
Security review sign-off and compliance checklist completed (if any customer requests)
Alerting: create Grafana dashboard panels for latency, errors, cost per token, and rerank score drift
Run mock failover and rollback drills with customer-success on paper runbook
Create customer communication draft for staged launch and deprecation timelines (if applicable)
scope_changes: 2026-02-22: Removed real-time rerank streaming from GA scope due to kernel-level prioritization unknowns; plan to ship batch rerank only
2026-02-28: Postponed multi-protocol support (gRPC) to post-GA; decided to stabilize REST surface first
2026-03-03: Accepted lightweight per-route QoS knobs (burst tokens) requested by Sales to support early enterprise customers
2026-03-08: Narrowed Embedded output format to deterministic vector dtype float32 for GA to reduce compatibility incidents; plan quantized variants in runtime-1.18
risks: Different models may have divergent tokenization behaviors that affect parity tests — mitigation: canonical tokenizer shim and token-normalization step in harness
Batching and KV cache interactions could cause higher latency tails for certain prompts — mitigation: isolate canary on single-tenant pools with controlled batch sizes
Backward compatibility with legacy SDK calls — mitigation: shim layer in SDKs and clear deprecation policy
Operational cost spikes during aggressive canary testing — mitigation: autoscaling caps and cost monitoring alerts
notes: Design review held 2026-02-18: agreed on chat turn format: {role, content, metadata} with optional tool-calls encoded as structured-objects
PM/Engineers agreed to enforce semantic versions in model labels to enable safe rollbacks
Decided to rely on existing Optimize recommendations for quantization at GA to avoid new surface
